all_found.desc: [BUG] landedTaskReviewRunIDs treats a task-done review as landed when its recorded head is an ancestor of (or equal to) the PR base, but task-done also reviews staged, working-tree and untracked content and records only the HEAD commit. The usual first chunk — branch from main, edit, run task-done before committing — records head == the main tip == BaseSHA, so `merge-base --is-ancestor H H` succeeds and that review of the branch's own unlanded work is moved to HistoricalRunIDs. Fails open: ProjectRecords files the run's log and blockers as historical, so pr-ready stops blocking on real, unfixed task-done findings for code that is now committed in base..HEAD — a false clear in a common workflow the CLAUDE.md lifecycle prescribes.

[ADVISORY] TestLandedTaskReviewRunIDsFailsClosed does not pin the SHA validation guards: deleting `validGitObjectID(head)` or the `!validGitObjectID(git.BaseSHA)` early return still passes, because the fixtures ('not-a-sha', 'unknown') are also rejected by git itself. A resolvable ref (e.g. HeadSHA: "main") would catch the head-guard mutant. Dropping the SHA validation would let a pack or run record whose head is a ref name like main/HEAD~1 be treated as landed with no failing test.

[BUG] A detached review (pack branch "") of this branch's own commit becomes history once a rebase or amend rewrites that commit: the old head still exists (reflog) but is no longer an ancestor of HEAD, so `!(branch=="" && inHistory)` returns true. The same happens when pr-ready itself runs on a detached HEAD (git.Branch empty, e.g. CI pull_request checkouts), where the own-branch guard can never fire. A real NEEDS_REVISION task-done blocker on this branch's own code stops blocking pr-ready after an ordinary rebase or on a detached checkout — fail-open, contradicting the stated fail-closed design; the verdict can differ between a developer's branch and CI.

[BUG] The fork-point guard compares the head with git.BaseSHA, which is the resolved --base tip (rev-parse), not merge-base(HEAD, base). Once main advances past the fork point F, a first chunk reviewed uncommitted on main (branch 'main', head F) before `git checkout -b`, or on a since-renamed branch, falls through to the final rule and is classified as history. The uncommitted-first-chunk blocker the previous fix meant to keep reopens as soon as the base advances or the branch is renamed; an unresolved task review of this PR's own work silently stops gating pr-ready.

[ADVISORY] The ARCHITECTURE bullet says detached reviews and unknown heads always stay current, but the code treats an unknown head naming another branch, and a detached review of an off-history commit, as history. The doc agents read first misstates the fail-closed rules.

[ADVISORY] landedTaskReviewRunIDs reads a context pack and runs up to three git subprocesses for every task-done log on every pr-ready run, before any path-overlap filter and without a timeout (~6s for this repo's 143 logs). Adds seconds to every pr-ready run, growing with history; a stalled git hangs the gate.

[BUG] flagTargetTaskReviewRunIDs retires every task-done log whose target starts with '-', resting on the claim that a run for a flag target cannot be made again — true only for --help/-h. main.go intercepts just those two and passes args[2] straight to taskdone.Create, and tasksource.Resolve accepts any non-path string as an advisory target, so `review task-done --verbose --base X` (or --base, --evidence, a mistyped flag with the target omitted) runs and records a full review of current work under a dash target. Reproduced: after `review task-done --verbose --base 851b84d` and `review task-done real-task` over the same commit, pr-ready blocked only on real-task; the --verbose run's identical current blocker was dropped with no human override — fail-open, against the stated design.

[ADVISORY] ARCHITECTURE.md and the review.go comment say, in the present tense, that any other stale blocker 'is cleared by a human-granted process override (#188)', but #188 is still open and `override request` cannot target committed-log blockers today. A reader following the doc tries override request/grant on a stale committed-log blocker, gets 'not found' with exit 0, and stays blocked.

[ADVISORY] The test file still carries scaffolding for the removed head/branch inference: it is named landed_task_review_test.go, historyRepo builds an unmerged 'old' branch standing in for a squash-merged branch and returns b and d that no caller uses, and the writeTaskDoneLog comment describes recording the head only in the pack. Readers are pointed at a 'landed commit' heuristic that no longer exists and may believe squash-merge cases are covered, inviting the removed inference back.

[BUG] The CLI refusal checks the raw target with strings.HasPrefix(args[2], "-") while flagTargetTaskReviewRunIDs matches strings.TrimSpace(log.Target), so `review task-done " --help"` (or "\t-h", "--help ") passes the refusal, runs a real review of current work, and records Target ` --help`, which pr-ready trims to --help and retires. Reproduced: the review's open blocker shows as 'does not block this target' while a control target keeps it blocking — any driver can create a real review whose blockers pr-ready silently ignores, with no override; the taskdone.Create Go API has no refusal at all.

[ADVISORY] The dash-target refusal guards only `review task-done`; `review epic-ready` takes args[2] as the target the same way, and `review epic-ready --verbose` records a real log under Target `--verbose` (reproduced). Epic-ready can still write flag-target logs nobody can re-run or supersede, and ARCHITECTURE's 'no new such logs can be written' holds only for task-done.

[ADVISORY] The test comment calls --help and -h 'the only flags that were ever recorded as targets (before #164)', but before this change any dash token in the target slot was recorded. A reader gets a false reason for the narrow match and could widen it back to every dash target, the regression the recheck caught.

[BUG] rerunCommand quotes a target containing $ or a backtick with strconv.Quote (Go double quotes), which the POSIX shell still expands; ;, &, *, ( and newlines are left unquoted. Copying the pack's Re-run command for such a target expands variables or runs command substitution and re-runs a different target (or an unintended command).

[BUG] The --help/-h retirement covers only task-done, but pre-#164 `review epic-ready --help` recorded a real epic-ready gate run under Target --help the same way (epicsource falls through to an advisory Source). Such a committed epic-ready log keeps blocking PRs that touch its paths and can never be re-run, since the CLI now refuses that target.

[ADVISORY] No test pins that taskdone.Create passes Target into shardpack.Header; deleting the line passes all tests (mutation-verified). A regression silently brings back a Re-run command the CLI refuses.

[ADVISORY] The retirement trusts the committed markdown Target line without RunRecordAuthenticated and ignores the verdict (retires ESCALATED). Hand-editing a real blocking log's Target to --help would retire its blockers without an override.

findings.issue_text: [BUG] In status --target <path>, a retired --help/-h log still counts as coverage via covers() when its HeadSHA is a branch commit, while retireRuns removes its blocker, so the path reports blocked:false with no real review. status --target (the hook's METAREVIEW_TARGET path) can clear a file only a pre-#164 --help run covered; before the delta it blocked.

rejected.desc: [BUG] The fix is narrower than #187's first AC (a review whose head is outside base..HEAD must not block). This repo squash-merges, so a task-done review made on a feature branch has a head that never becomes an ancestor of main; such heads stay in the current set. Of 143 committed task-done logs, 117 have heads that are not ancestors of main (15 not in the object store at all). Later PRs that touch the covered paths of those squash-merged task reviews are still blocked by blockers that can never be resolved — the #187 failure — and the ARCHITECTURE bullet overstates the coverage; the test uses only a head on main.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] internal/shardpack writes a '## Re-run' line `metareview review <scope> --base <sha>` into every shard prompt pack; for task-done that omits the target, so args[2] is "--base" and the new refusal rejects the documented re-run command (before, it recorded a bogus '--base' review).
